question: Does extending a FAST-encoded future while preserving its executed action prefix change reconstruction of that prefix, and can full-chunk error hide that change?
claim_boundary: Expert-action codec round trip only. No policy inference, simulator rollout, contact measurement, task success, VLA improvement, or learned tokenizer comparison.

fast.implementation: load reviewed official processor and tokenizer locally inside Docker; check against independent scipy DCT round trip

sampling.anchors: start at frame 0, stride long_horizon, at most 8 complete non-overlapping long windows per episode; no padding, no episode crossing
sampling.unit: episode; windows within an episode are dependent. Datasets are separate and are not pooled as independent robot embodiments.
sampling.normalization: per-dimension q01/q99 fitted only on episodes 0..4; affine map to [-1,1], no clipping; report out-of-range and degenerate dimensions
sampling.limit: Public simulation demonstration exports; no success-label qualification and no policy-training holdout claim. First episode IDs are a convenience sample.

comparators.FAST_short: encode complete 1-second chunk; decode all tokens; evaluate full chunk and first 0.2 seconds
comparators.FAST_long: same start/prefix and scale, encode complete 2-second chunk; decode all tokens; evaluate full chunk and same first 0.2 seconds
comparators.pointwise: round each normalized action to nearest 0.1, no clipping; causal invariance sanity baseline, NOT matched bitrate or a policy baseline
comparators.identity: exact copied trajectory control; expected zero error

metrics: per-window full normalized MSE and prefix normalized MSE; episode means
prefix RMS difference between FAST_short and FAST_long reconstructions of the identical prefix
pairwise full-versus-prefix preference disagreement with tie tolerance 1e-12
per-dimension errors, raw-unit prefix MAE with no mixed-unit sum
actual BPE token counts and count*log2(vocab_size) as a nominal code-length proxy, NOT measured VLA latency
input hashes, decoded shape, BPE round-trip parity, clipping and failure counts

decision_rules.correctness_stop: nonfinite data, missing episode/frame continuity, zero quantile width, coefficient floor clipping, decode mismatch, or failed controls => no scientific result for affected dataset; diagnose explicitly
decision_rules.null: If identity and pointwise controls pass and observed prefix effect is negligible or has no stable episode pattern, record a weak/negative diagnostic; do not expand compute automatically.
decision_rules.explore: Nonzero prefix dependency or preference disagreement establishes only an offline codec property. Prefix RMS >0.01 normalized units is a predeclared descriptive flag, not a robot safety or publication threshold.
decision_rules.no_method_go: Regardless of outcome, do not claim a new tokenizer, new theorem, policy failure cause, or task improvement. Strong OAT/REALFAST/discrete-controller/streaming-codec precedents require a differentiated downstream result.

external_feedback: not requested or received; prepare review questions only
